html:
Italian Somaliland was the colony of Italy on the Indian Ocean coast of the Horn of Africa, in what is now central and southern Somalia, from 1889 to 1941.

Italy came in through treaties. In 1889 the sultanates of Hobyo and Majeerteen in the north accepted Italian protection. In the south Italy took the old Benadir ports, Mogadishu, Merca and Barawa, in the 1890s, then pushed inland along the Shebelle and Jubba rivers. Somali clans fought back near Merca, and the Dervish movement of Mohammed Abdullah Hassan resisted in the north until 1920. Real Italian control stayed near the coast until then.

  • 1925: Britain handed over Jubaland, west of the Jubba, as a reward for Italy's side in World War I.
  • 1927: the northern sultanates came under direct rule.
  • 1935 to 1936: the colony was a base for the invasion of Ethiopia, and then became part of Italian East Africa.
  • 1941: British troops occupied it.

Italy returned to run it as a United Nations trust territory from 1950. In 1960 it joined British Somaliland to form independent Somalia.
sum: Italian Somaliland was the colony of Italy on the Indian Ocean coast of the Horn of Africa, in what is now central and southern Somalia, from 1889 to 1941.
